newsitem.title: JAPAN: M'bishi Oil,General Sekiyu mull supply cooperation.
newsitem.headline: M'bishi Oil,General Sekiyu mull supply cooperation.

text.p: Mitsubishi Oil Co Ltd and General Sekiyu KK are expected to begin supplying each other with oil products as part of efforts to cut costs, a Mitsubishi Oil spokesman said on Thursday.
The two companies are holding talks on supplying each other with 600,000 kilolitres (kl) of oil products and an agreement is expected, he said.
"We are holding negotiations with that goal in mind," the Mitsubishi Oil spokesman said.
The move would help cut costs by about one billion yen a year for the two oil refining and distribution companies.
The oil products that will be exchanged are kerosene, gas oil and gasoline including high-octane gasoline.
The volume to be cross-supplied -- 600,000 kl -- represents about four percent of Mitsubishi Oil's and about 10 percent of General Sekiyu's annual sales of the three oil products, the spokesman said.
The two companies will each close two oil storage tanks after an agreement is reached, the Mitsubishi Oil spokesman said, although he could not say when the agreement would be concluded.
Japan's oil industry continues to suffer from poor profit margins a year after industry deregulation in April 1996, when oil firms lost their virtually exclusive right to import petroleum products.
The planned move by Mitsubishi Oil and General Sekiyu is the latest in a growing trend within the industry to build business alliances and streamline operations.
Mitsubishi Oil and Showa Shell Sekiyu KK, owned 50 percent by the Royal Dutch/Shell Group, said in February they were thinking of merging their refining divisions.
General Sekiyu is owned 49 percent by Exxon Corp. --Tokyo Energy Desk +81-3-5473-3706
